checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is transaction sender identity protected against signature spoofing via recover_sender?

reachability.notes: An attacker crafts a transaction with a forged or malleable signature. If recover_sender has an edge-case bug, the attacker could impersonate another account and spend its funds.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Locate the recover_sender function implementation. 2. Review signature validation logic for ECDSA (v, r, s) components. 3. Verify EIP-2 compliance: check that high-s values are rejected (s must be <= secp256k1n/2). 4. Test with malleable signatures: for a valid signature (v, r, s), craft (v', r, secp256k1n - s) and verify rejection. 5. Test edge cases: v = 27/28 handling, r = 0, s = 0, r >= secp256k1n, s >= secp256k1n. 6. Verify ecrecover returns expected address for known test vectors. 7. Attempt to craft a signature that recovers to a different address than the actual signer.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0005, Trust Boundary: tb-001. Signature spoofing allows complete account takeover - attacker can impersonate any account, transfer funds, and increment nonce.

checklist.title: Verify EIP-2 Signature Malleability Protection in recover_sender

reachability.notes: An attacker crafts a transaction with a forged or malleable signature. If recover_sender has an edge-case bug, the attacker could impersonate another account and spend its funds.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify where EIP-2 s-value check is implemented. 2. Verify the check uses the correct half-order constant (secp256k1n/2 = 0x7FFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF5D576E7357A4501DDFE92F46681B20A0). 3. Test boundary: signature with s exactly at the limit. 4. Test with s = secp256k1n/2 + 1 (should be rejected). 5. Verify that transaction replay with flipped s-value is impossible.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0005, Supporting check for EIP-2 compliance. Malleable signatures could allow transaction replay or sender impersonation.

checklist.title: Verify Canonical Address Derivation from Recovered Public Key

reachability.notes: An attacker crafts a transaction with a forged or malleable signature. If recover_sender has an edge-case bug, the attacker could impersonate another account and spend its funds.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Trace the flow from ecrecover result to final sender address. 2. Verify Keccak-256 hash is applied to the recovered public key (without the 0x04 prefix). 3. Verify the address is derived from the last 20 bytes of the hash. 4. Test with known public key / address pairs from test vectors. 5. Check for any truncation or byte-order issues in address derivation.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0005, Supporting check for address derivation. Incorrect derivation could map valid signatures to wrong addresses.

checklist.title: Verify P2P Transaction Propagation Does Not Bypass Signature Validation

reachability.notes: An attacker crafts a transaction with a forged or malleable signature. If recover_sender has an edge-case bug, the attacker could impersonate another account and spend its funds.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify all P2P entry points for transaction submission. 2. Verify signature validation occurs before any state modification or propagation. 3. Check that transactions with invalid signatures are rejected at the network layer. 4. Test by submitting transactions via P2P with forged signatures and verify immediate rejection. 5. Ensure no caching of sender address occurs before validation.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0005, Supporting check for P2P entry point (SG-006). Actor nodes: actor-tx-sender, actor-evm.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is RLP encoding deterministic and collision-free across all client implementations?

reachability.notes: Multiple subgraphs rely on RLP for serialization. If an attacker can craft a payload that encodes differently across implementations, clients would compute different block hashes and diverge.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify all RLP encoding/decoding entry points in the P2P layer. 2. Review the RLP encoding implementation for edge cases (empty lists, nested structures, large integers, maximum length fields). 3. Compare encoding output across multiple client implementations (Geth, Nethermind, Besu, Erigon) for identical input blocks. 4. Test with boundary values: zero-length strings, maximum-length payloads, deeply nested structures. 5. Verify that decode(encode(x)) == x for all valid inputs (round-trip consistency). 6. Attempt to craft payloads where leading zeros or alternative representations could produce different encodings. 7. Check for integer encoding ambiguity (e.g., encoding 0x00 vs empty bytes).
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0006, Trust Boundaries: tb-002, tb-005, tb-010. Covers actors: P2P peer, block proposer, EVM. Non-deterministic encoding causes consensus splits - different clients accept different blocks, fragmenting the network.

checklist.title: Verify Block Hash Consistency: Do all clients compute identical hashes for the same block data?

reachability.notes: Multiple subgraphs rely on RLP for serialization. If an attacker can craft a payload that encodes differently across implementations, clients would compute different block hashes and diverge.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Select a sample of real mainnet blocks with varying complexity. 2. Re-encode each block using each client's RLP implementation. 3. Compute the block hash from each client's encoding. 4. Verify all hashes match exactly. 5. Test with blocks containing: (a) transactions with unusual gas values, (b) empty uncle lists vs null uncle lists, (c) extra data fields at maximum length, (d) withdrawal lists (post-Shanghai). 6. Document any discrepancies and trace to specific encoding differences.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0006, Supporting check for block hash computation which depends on deterministic RLP encoding.

checklist.title: Verify RLP Collision Resistance: Can two distinct blocks B1 != B2 produce identical RLP encodings?

reachability.notes: Multiple subgraphs rely on RLP for serialization. If an attacker can craft a payload that encodes differently across implementations, clients would compute different block hashes and diverge.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Review RLP specification for injectivity guarantees (RFC compliance). 2. Analyze if different field orderings or optional fields could produce same encoding. 3. Test: Create two semantically different blocks and verify their encodings differ. 4. Specifically test: (a) blocks differing only in timestamp by 1 second, (b) blocks differing only in extra data content, (c) blocks differing only in transaction ordering. 5. Attempt to find collision by brute-forcing small payload variations. 6. Verify the encoding scheme is prefix-free (no valid encoding is a prefix of another).
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0006, Invariant verification: For all B1 != B2, rlp.encode(B1) != rlp.encode(B2).

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is keccak256 hash computation and comparison correctly implemented across all block integrity checks?

reachability.notes: Keccak256 provides 256-bit security. A collision is computationally infeasible with current technology, but an implementation bug in hash computation or comparison could be exploitable.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify all code paths that compute keccak256 hashes for block headers, state roots, receipt roots, and transaction roots. 2. Review hash comparison logic for timing-safe equality checks and correct byte ordering. 3. Verify that parent hash verification uses the exact same hash computation as block production. 4. Test with crafted blocks containing near-collision prefixes to verify comparison strictness. 5. Audit for any truncation or partial hash comparisons that could weaken security. 6. Check for off-by-one errors in hash buffer handling that could cause incomplete hash computation. 7. Verify hash inputs are correctly serialized (RLP encoding) before hashing.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0007, Trust Boundaries: tb-002, tb-005. Primary element: SG-002. Actors: block-proposer, state-db. This is a CRITICAL boundary check because keccak256 hash integrity is fundamental to all block verification. While cryptographic collision is computationally infeasible, implementation bugs in hash computation or comparison could enable block forgery.

checklist.title: Verify Block Hash Computation: Are all inputs to block hash correctly serialized and included?

reachability.notes: Keccak256 provides 256-bit security. A collision is computationally infeasible with current technology, but an implementation bug in hash computation or comparison could be exploitable.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Review RLP encoding of block headers to ensure all required fields are included in canonical order. 2. Verify that no fields are omitted or duplicated in hash preimage. 3. Test that hash changes when any single field is modified. 4. Check for consistent handling of optional/nil fields across different block types. 5. Verify hash computation is deterministic across all code paths.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0007. Supporting check for block hash integrity. Missing or incorrectly ordered fields in hash preimage could allow two different blocks to produce the same hash.

checklist.title: Verify Parent Hash Chain Integrity: Is parent hash verification performed before block acceptance?

reachability.notes: Keccak256 provides 256-bit security. A collision is computationally infeasible with current technology, but an implementation bug in hash computation or comparison could be exploitable.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the code path where incoming blocks have their parent hash verified. 2. Confirm that parent hash must match an existing block's computed hash, not just a stored value. 3. Test with blocks claiming a valid parent hash but containing modified parent data. 4. Verify that orphan blocks (with unknown parents) are handled correctly and not prematurely accepted. 5. Check for race conditions where parent could be removed between verification and block insertion.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0007. Supporting check for chain integrity. Failure to properly verify parent hash could allow chain splits or reorganizations with forged blocks.

checklist.title: Verify State/Receipt/Transaction Root Integrity: Are Merkle roots correctly computed and verified?

reachability.notes: Keccak256 provides 256-bit security. A collision is computationally infeasible with current technology, but an implementation bug in hash computation or comparison could be exploitable.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Review Merkle Patricia Trie implementation for correct keccak256 usage at each node level. 2. Verify that transaction root is computed over RLP-encoded transaction list in correct order. 3. Verify that receipt root is computed over RLP-encoded receipt list matching transaction order. 4. Verify that state root reflects all state changes from block execution. 5. Test with blocks containing valid-looking roots but incorrect underlying data. 6. Check for vulnerabilities in proof verification that could accept invalid proofs.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0007. Supporting check for Merkle root integrity. State root, receipt root, and transaction root all use keccak256 in Merkle Patricia Tries. Implementation bugs could allow state manipulation.
